### Standards established (from `expanded/learnings.md`, preserved and applied here)
- Every entry carries name, attributed definition, formula if captured, representative values, source/date, stated data source, and caveats. Don't guess missing formulas or sources.
- Denominators, filters, sample windows, and minimum qualifiers are first-class fields (e.g., true target share = % of **team pass attempts**, not targets; Statyx "last_3" = NQ = not qualified).
- Approximate chart transcriptions stay approximate — never promoted to canonical values.
- Distinct denominators mean distinct metrics (success-rate conventions don't merge across sources).
- Reposts and new cuts of existing metrics are revisits, not new metrics; the "also covered in sweep report.md" flags above keep the attribution straight.
- Vendor disclosure is an attributed claim, not independent supply-chain verification (e.g., "750+ NFL data points", OddsPapi 350+ books, SumerSports' lead claims).
- Public reading does not grant redistribution rights; respect targets' licenses (Firecrawl rule 7).
- Research doctrine: public surfaces only; provenance on everything; CONFIRMED/INFERRED/UNVERIFIED labels; no fabricated URLs/endpoints; no hallucinated schemas/formulas; extract, don't summarize.
- Proprietary charts shouldn't be republished as GSE data; the clean reusable foundation is nflverse.

### Gotchas
-

[part 119] **OddsPapi traps** (vendor-documented): `hasOdds=false` on finished fixtures is expected, not missing data; identical price tuples must be grouped empirically (`cloneOf` doesn't track all duplicates); tournamentId lifts the 10-day fixture window; historical-odds retention disputed (docs say Jan 2026, independent probe ~90 days) — resolve live before backfill; "free" endpoints still 429 after plan exhaustion.
- **Close semantics**: no `is_closing` field — close = last active snapshot with `createdAt < kickoff`; Pinnacle prices in-play so a pre-KO cutoff is mandatory.
- **Pinnacle `limit`** per snapshot = max stake = a confidence signal no other free source carries — persist it.
- **persist `externalProviders`** at fixture ingest — collapses entity resolution across every downstream feed keyed to any listed provider.
- **Key hygiene**: OddsPapi key is a query param — never log the query string; 429 body carries `error.retryMs` as valid JSON — honor it.
- **ESPN public endpoints**: undocumented, unstable; UA behavior changes responses (403 browser UA vs 200 plain curl).
- **Do not retry**: rbsdm.com (failed to load in mission), statrankings provider inference from FTN/Kevin Adams link, fantasy-points paywalled articles.
- **Manual charting QA** (from b_peters12 recon): store observed geometry separately from inferred team terminology; double-chart, adjudicate, compute inter-rater reliability, retain timestamped film evidence, version the codebook.
- **Under-center cut**: needs explicit treatment of no-plays, spikes, kneels, penalties, pistol; exact nflverse field names unverified.
- **StatRankings JS inventory** (`statrankings/js/`): 103 files; controllers reveal app features — stat builder (`stat_builder_player_search_controller`), projection overrides (`projection_override_controller`), survivor grid (`survivor_grid_model`, `survivor_map_controller`), implied probability (`implied_probability`), market search (`market_search_controller`), depth-chart overrides, coverage shell controllers, paywall modal (`paywall_modal_controller`, `unlock_modal_controller`), PDF export (`pdf_export_controller`). Controller names = UI capabilities evidence, **not public API endpoints**. `nfl-urls.txt` = 1,148 paths; `methodology-definitions.json` = 673 glossary definitions (prose, no proprietary formulas — ARBY/Havoc/PROE+/xFP definitions absent).
- The 2026 Fantasy Points Advanced Matchups article was paywalled and not accessed; SumerSports lead claims (LB/DI/edge tables, 2022 preseason/postseason, WELCOME15) not independently confirmed — keep flagged as unconfirmed.

## 7. LESSONS (builder-oriented)

- **Composite-metric construction patterns observed in the wild:** ARBY (65% ARBY / 35% RB YPC, 65% prior-year / 35% current-year, 50/50 offense-defense; TNF version adds game-weighting 5/2 across windows); benbbaldwin pass-protection composite (PFF 40% / SIS blown-block 40% / ESPN PBWR 20%, each source re-scaled 0–100 before blending); SamHoppen Week 3 composite power ratings (mean of 6 sources as expected spread vs. average, with per-team std dev as the disagreement measure); ThunderDan PROJ YPPR (prior-year baseline × projected opponent coverage splits, 80/20 old/new blend); RaritosFootball Nota (EPA + success rate + pressure → 1–10 with attack/defense sub-ratings). When a builder reverse-engineers a public composite, look for this shape: weighted blend of public/paid inputs + a prior-year anchor + a normalization step.
- **Most of the signal is vendor-gated; the cons

[part 133] truction is what matters.** The valuable reverse-engineering targets are the open methodology + construction patterns, not the charted data (FTN, PFF, Statyx, SIS, ESPN PBWR are all gated).
- **New labels can surface without definitions:** "9YOE" (GridironInfo, 9/22) has no definition — unusable until the author defines it; flag as watch-item, do not guess.
- **Snap-qualification and tiny-sample traps:** the SumerSports PRWR min-25-snaps leaderboard was led by players with ~5 and ~3 snaps (Hunt 29.6%, Muhammad 27.3%) — the filter denominator was unclear from the screenshot. Treat unqualified or small-sample leaderboards as provisional; gate win-rate metrics on snap volume.
- **Chart-reads are approximate; formulas are exact.** Browser-task reads of rendered charts carry per-cell transcription risk — PARTIAL/APPROX flags exist for a reason. Author-stated formulas (ARBY's footer, ThunderDan's 80/20 blend, benbbaldwin's 40/40/20) are the reverse-engineering-grade material.
- **Position-aware baselines:** WillBrinson's caveat on the rushing-EPA chart — QB rushing (scrambles, situational runs) is not comparable to traditional RB rushing; keep position-aware reference lines.
- **Same caveat applies to explosive-play counts (@DETROlTLions313, Sep 23):** the Claude-built query excluded QB runs — Seattle's allowed 10+ rushes read 2 in the dashboard vs 4 manually counted (Drake Maye 16 and 10, Stevenson 12, Bam Knight 18). Any explosive-rush pipeline must explicitly include or exclude QB runs and say which; verify against other sources before comparing.
- **The backup-QB lesson (Keenum study):** no positional tell — rusty Keenum is not a TE guy or checkdown guy (WR 62.2% / TE 20.1% / RB 17.6% in return games). The "safety blanket" is role-based (slot / receiving RB / X) and follows the roster and scheme, not the QB. For DFS stacking or prop angles on backup QBs, identify the scheme's designated guy, not a position.
- **Descriptive ≠ predictive:** BAL posted a 16.6% higher success rate than NO and still lost (second-largest net success-rate upset since 2022); success-rate edges don't guarantee outcomes. Keep the engine's descriptive inputs separated from its outcome predictions.
- **Fourth-down aggressiveness as regime indicator:** 2026 W1–2 ≈ 16% vs 2025 ≈ 21% (ngreenberg/TruMedia). Early-season samples are small — don't over-fit; author's framing ("small-sample blip or new normal?") is the right posture.
- **nflverse pbp has no alignment data:** slot/X/Y/Z attribution needs charting data (FTN/PFF/Statyx). The Keenum blanket-role analysis required general-knowledge alignment notes — flag that boundary explicitly in any engine input.
- **Garrett's process lesson (Sept 24 pool notes):** his reads were directionally right and the actuals were slightly better than he remembered (DAL 29.7 FPG to TEs, not 27; Andrews 24.5% share, not 25%) — verify numerically before fading or following, but don't dismiss his directional instincts.
- **The no-code pipeline recipe is engine-replicable (@DETROlTLions313):** natural-language prompt → Claude → RStudio + nflreadr → BigQuery → Grafana. End-to-end verified by a third party. Cumulative EPA by play number (not by week) is a trend shape the engine can mirror for any quarterback.

## 3. NFL injury/concussion protocol notes (modeling-relevant)

**Source:** `nfl-protocols/injury-concussion-protocol.md` (compiled 2026-09-21; CONFIRMED = official
NFL/NFLPA documents; REPORTED = secondary reporting).

### 3.1 Concussion game-day sideline evaluation (Rev. Oct 2022 — current)

- **Initiators:** ATC, booth ATC, team physician, NFL official, coach, teammate, or UNC (Unaffiliated
  Neurotrauma Consultant). Player immediately removed to sideline (or stabilized on field).
- **Sideline survey:** No-Go check, History of Event, Concussion Signs/Symptoms, Maddock's Questions,
  Video Review, Focused Neurological Exam (cervical spine ROM/pain, speech, gait, eye movements +
  pupillary exam). Team Physician + UNC.
- **No-Go list (current):** loss of consciousness (LOC), **ataxia**, confusion, amnesia. Ataxia =
  "abnormality of balance/stability, motor coordination or dysfunctional speech caused by a
  neurological issue." Added October 2022 after the Tua Tagovailoa investigation; replaced "gross
  motor instability" and eliminated the "alternative explanation" loophole — ataxia observed at
  any point = no return, no exceptions.
- **No-Go sign at ANY point → NO RETURN TO PLAY** (rest of game minimum).
- Normal sideline survey + "benign" video review → may return.
- Any positive/inconclusive/suspicious → locker room full NFL SCAT + complete neurological exam;
  "Questionable to return — concussion".
- Progressive/worsening symptoms or abnormal locker room exam → NO RETURN TO PLAY.
- **"Madden Rule":** once a concussion is diagnosed, the player may not return to that game.
- **No set timeframe for return** — every concussion unique. **Daily monitoring** (or more frequent)
  through the entire protocol required.

### 3.2 Return-to-Participation Protocol — the five steps

**Gate rule (every step transition):** advance ONLY after demonstrating tolerance of ALL activities in
the current step without recurre

[part 142] nce of observed/reported concussion signs/symptoms; recurrence →
stop, return to the **prior step**. Player must stay at pre-concussion baseline during exertion
AND a "reasonable period" after (Team Physician decides). Progression **may be accelerated** by
severity/time to baseline.
**Clearance authority:** Head Team Physician (or designated Team Physician) decides; **ALL
return-to-full-participation decisions must be confirmed by the Independent Neurological Consultant
(INC)**. INC must be informed at diagnosis. Final clearance = team medical staff decision
**confirmed by the INC**.

| Step | Name | Core content | Observable leak |
|------|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Rest and Recovery | Physical + relative cognitive rest; limit electronics/meetings until signs/symptoms + neuro exam (cognitive + balance) return to baseline | "DNP — Concussion" on practice report; "Out" on game status |
| 2 | Light Aerobic Exercise | Graduated CV exercise (bike, treadmill) under direct medical-staff oversight; dynamic stretching + balance; may attend meetings/film | DNP → Limited |
| 3 | Continued Aerobic + Strength | Increased supervised CV (may mimic sport-specific); supervised strength training; non-contact sport-specific conditioning (COD, cone drills) | Limited |
| 4 | Football-Specific Activities | Non-contact football (throwing, catching, running, position-specific). Strictly non-contact — no contact with players OR objects (dummies, sleds) | Limited (non-contact) |
| 5 | Full Football Activity / Clearance | After tolerating all above + meetings + conditioning + non-contact practice: (a) physician clears full contact → full practice; (b) clears to full participation; (c) INC examines, receives ALL reports incl. neurocognitive tests; (d) INC confirms → cleared for next game/practice | Full practice; off injury report / no game designation |

**Neurocognitive testing gates:** may be introduced any time after Step 1 or during Steps 2–3, MUST
be completed **before contact activities**; interpreted by team's neuropsychology consultant; if not
back to baseline → repeat at interval (typically 48 hours); Team Physician must evaluate
non-injury causes of any decrement. May do non-contact with abnormal testing; may NOT proceed to
contact until baseline OR physician determines non-concussion cause.

### 3.3 General injury track — practice participation + game status

- **Practice report designations:** DNP (did not participate), LP (limited participation), FP (full
  participation). Veteran rest / non-injury absence may be listed DNP/LP with labeled reason
  (e.g., NIR-Rest) — rest days permitted but must be labeled.
- **Cadence:** standard Sunday game → practice reports Wednesday, Thursday, Friday (Thursday/
  Saturday/Monday games shift the schedule).
- **Game status (binding):** **Out** = will not play; **Doubtful** = unlikely to play;
  **Questionable** = uncertain to play. Deadline **4:00 PM ET, two days before game day** (Friday
  for Sunday; Wednesday for Thursday). Certain-to-play players are removed from the report
  (explainable to the league; discipline possible if then deactivated). Status changes after the
  report must be re-reported.
- **"Probable" eliminated in 2016** — ~95% of "probable" players played, making it meaningless.
  Any availability question defaults to "Questionable". The separate "Out" category was also
  removed from the **practice** report.
- **Final word:** official inactive list (~90 minutes before kickoff).

### 3.4 Enforcement history (documented)

| Year | Club/individual | Violation | Penalty |
|------|-----------------|-----------|---------|
| 2025 (Oct) | Ravens ($100K) | Lamar Jackson listed Full Participant Friday while taking only scout-team reps (hamstring); retroactively downgraded to Limited, then ruled Out | $100K club fine; negligence — no draft picks |
| 2023 | Falcons ($75K) + HC Arthur Smith ($25K) | Bijan Robinson played limited Week 7 role with no injury designation; Saturday-night illness never added | $75K / $25K |
| 2019 | Steelers ($75K) + HC Mike Tomlin ($25K) | Ben Roethlisberger's elbow injury not accurately listed on practice report | $75K / $25K |

League rules language (quoted): *"A violation of the policy may result in Commissioner discipline,
which may include a fine on the involved club, fines or suspensions of involved individuals, as
well as the possible forfeiture of draft choices by the involved club."*

### 3.5 Concussion vs. general injury — struct

[part 143] ural differences

| Dimension | Concussion | General injury |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| Governing doc | NFL Head/Neck/Spine Committee protocols (+ NFLPA) | NFL Injury Report Policy (league ops) |
| Mandatory progression | Yes — 5 graduated steps + regression on recurrence | No — team medical judgment |
| Same-game return | Prohibited once diagnosed; prohibited on any No-Go sign | Permitted if medically cleared |
| Independent clearance | Required — INC must confirm Team Physician | None |
| Cognitive testing | Mandatory neurocognitive baseline before contact; 48-hr retest | Not required |
| Minimum timeline | None fixed — step structure + INC gate makes sub-week returns rare | None — DNP Friday → play Sunday possible |
| Daily monitoring | Required | Not required |
| Observable signal | Practice participation (DNP→LP→FP = Steps 1–4); "Full" + no designation = Step 5 + INC done | Practice trend (Wed→Thu→Fri) primary; game status binding |
| Reporting surface | Same injury report | Same injury report |

### 3.6 GSE encoding notes (protocol-derived, not media-derived)

1. **Concussion = absorbing state until INC confirms.** Any "concussion" designation means the
   5-step progression is running. No legitimate same-week shortcut: beat-reporter speculation
   about a concussed player "practicing Friday" describes at most Step 3–4 (non-contact).
2. **The observable leak for concussions is practice participation.** DNP (concussion) → LP
   (concussion) maps to Steps 1–4. Encode the *transition*, not the beat writer's verb.
3. **Ataxia = automatic game-ender.** Since Oct 2022, any observed ataxia = no return, no
   exceptions, no "back injury" alternative explanation. Video showing it with a return = protocol
   violation story.
4. **For general injuries, the trend beats the label.** DNP→LP→FP = improving; FP→LP→DNP =
   deteriorating. Friday's designation is binding (Out = out; Doubtful ≈ out in practice).
   "Questionable" is the mandated bucket for *any* uncertainty since Probable was killed in 2016 —
   not a 50/50 coin flip, it's a range.
5. **Rest vs. injury is labeled.** NIR-Rest / veteran rest days are permitted and labeled — don't
   model a rest DNP as an injury signal.
6. **Status changes must be re-reported.** A player added/downgraded after the Friday 4 PM ET
   report is itself a signal (the Bijan Robinson lesson — and a finable offense if hidden).

### 6.1 Architectural blueprint — calibrated, tracking-decoupled sports probability engine

**Source doc thesis:** Build an elite, well-calibrated sports probability engine WITHOUT paying for
live 10Hz spatial tracking (licensing "typically exceeding hundreds of thousands of dollars
annually"; BDB/token-gated NGS scraping for commercial use violates non-commercial licensing/ToS).
Decouple the spatial tracking pipeline from the uncertainty/calibration engine. Harvest edge from:
(1) advanced uncertainty quantification, (2) distribution-free conformal calibration,
(3) continuous margin density evaluation (not point probabilities), (4) market microstructure
exploitation (Shin devigging, B-spline steam detection, state-transition latency arbitrage).
Raw coordinates via non-commercial datasets for offline method validation only; learned
architectures refit onto owned/open-source event data (nflverse) before anything commercial.
Three-tiered roadmap (Rungs 1–3: data integrity → predictive calibration → priceable execution),
fail-closed gates at every step. Unifying principle: survival under Knightian uncertainty —
no deep learning and no execution until data geometry and finite-sample guarantees are
"mathematically ab

[part 148] solute."

**Key methods/gates:**
- **Performance model and market model kept DECOUPLED** — closing lines are never input features
  to team-strength models (would just parrot the oddsmaker). Prevents target leakage.
- **Physical-plausibility gating (Rung 1):** flag any player movement exceeding **13 m/s** as
  fatally corrupt (not an outlier); market series: reject non-finite timestamps
  (`SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError`); scan for fixture triplication, phantom matches from API timeouts,
  corrupted consensus metrics (e.g., public betting percentages pinned at exactly 1.0000 across a
  full MLB run-line slate); wind direction must not be naively averaged (mean of 0° and 359°
  wrongly yields 180°) — store as categorical strings or directional cosines. Design assumptions:
  market-data violation rate "well above five percent"; spatial datasets "approaching 19%" corrupt
  (approximate, attributed to raw-event-log audits).
- **Margin densities, not point probabilities:** migrate fully to densities — a density prices every
  alternate spread/total/teaser, is the only sound basis for pricing middles, maps where the
  market's whole probability curve diverges from fair. Valuation: true value = integral of the
  expected-points curve g_EP over the density f(y|s). Construction: map historical residual std
  onto the current point estimate → widened Gaussian baseline density → full PDF answering "what
  are fair odds at -1.5 through -4.5", not just "does -3.5 hold EV."
- **CRPS as the primary proper scoring rule:** abandon MAE (ignores variance) and binary Brier
  (can't evaluate continuous margins). CRPS = integral over x of [F(x) − 1{x ≥ y}]² dx. Gaussian
  closed form via Φ(z), φ(z). **Operational gate:** new density model must show CRPS improvement of
  <0.01 on ≥150 settled spreads vs. widened Gaussian baseline before live execution.
- **Conformal honesty package:** no clamped CQR; Jackknife+ (coverage 1−2α → exactly 80% at

### 6.2 Conformal prediction, small-sample calibration, sports market probabilities — audit

**Thesis:** standard point forecasters and uncalibrated quantile regressions exhibit systematic
finite-sample under-coverage whenever feature dimension is non-trivial relative to sample size.
Wrap every publishable prediction in distribution-free conformal machinery; operate FAIL-CLOSED:
whenever the calibration sample is too small to certify the nominal quantile, emit an infinite
interval or refuse to publish (No-Bet), never clamp the quantile to the largest observed residual.
Central slogan: "eliminate fake tightness."

**Exact formulas:**
- **CQR** (Romano, Patterson & Candès 2019, arXiv:1905.03222): E_i =
  max(q_α_lo(X_i) − Y_i, Y_i − q_α_hi(X_i)); Q_{1−α}(E; I₂) = ⌈(1−α)(|I₂|+1)⌉-th largest
  element; C(X_{n+1}) = [q_α_lo − Q, q_α_hi + Q]. Guarantee P(Y∈C) ≥ 1−α under exchangeability.
- **Jackknife+** (Barber, Candès, Ramdas & Tibshirani 2019, arXiv:1905.02928): LOO residuals
  R_i^LOO = |Y_i − μ_{−i}(X_i)|; interval [q_α^−(μ_{−i}(X_{n+1}) − R_i^LOO),
  q_{1−α}^+(μ_{−i}(X_{n+1}) + R_i^LOO)]; guarantee ≥ 1−2α.
- **Split conformal** (Angelopoulos & Bates 2021, arXiv:2107.07511): q_hat = ⌈(n+1)(1−α)⌉/n
  empirical quantile; level δ must satisfy δ ≥ 1/(n+1) (Dietterich & Hostetler 2022,
  arXiv:2206.04860).
- **The n=5, α=0.10 hand computation:** inflation factor (1−α)(1+1/n) = 0.90×1.20 = 1.08; rank
  k = ⌈6×0.90⌉ = 6 > 5 → quantile at 1.08 (>1.0) yields +∞. Minimum n for α=0.10: n ≥ ⌈1/α⌉−1 = 9.
  Clamped coverage = 5/6 ≈ 83.33%; under-coverage defect 6.67%.
- **ACI:** α_{t+1} = α_t + γ(α − err_t), err_t = 1{Y_t ∉ C_t}. Asymptotic coverage under
  arbitrary shifts; NO finite-sample marginal guarantee over an 18-week NFL schedule.
- **EnbPI:** aggregates bootstrap ensemble forecasts over rolling horizons.
- **SPCI:** s_t = f(s_{t−1},…,s_{t−p}) + e_t; valid finite-sample intervals provided the residual
  time series remains stationary.
- **Rolling-origin CP:** calibrate against m most recent pseudo-OOS forecast errors; for a
  structured 272-game NFL season, sliding window m = 32 to 64 games.
- **SPI:** augments scarce calibration sets with synthetic samples from domain priors.
- **Binary calibration:** Platt scaling; Isotonic Regression (PAVA) — requires pre-coalescence of
  tied scores (internal GSE note [16]: aggregate equal-score labels and weights before PAV);
  Venn-Abers (generalized, van der Laan & Alaa 2025, arXiv:2502.05676) → [p₀, p₁];
  impossibility result (Barber et al. 2020, EJS): bounded-length distribution-free CIs for π(X)
  impossible without structural assumptions.
- **Calibration metrics/gates:** ECE — fail-closed above 0.05; Brier; Venn-Abers width — PROVEN
  gate: re

[part 150] fuse moneyline pick / No-Bet if p₁−p₀ > 0.20; Clopper-Pearson exact binomial CIs for
  sample win rates — withhold public performance displays until n ≥ 30 (internal PR #454:
  headline + per-bucket 95% Clopper-Pearson on decided picks, five equal-mass + equal-width
  quantile buckets); CLV — partition models into release-time snapshots; incorporating
  near-game-time lines into training leaks future information; Mondrian conformal — subgroup
  calibration across sports for equalized marginal coverage; Nested Conformal / QOOB (2019):
  F_t(x) = {y : score(x,y) ≤ t}, calibrating t via OOB cross-splits.
- **Linear QR under-coverage bias** (Lin, Trivedi & Sun 2021): for α>0.5 and small d/n, the
  α-quantile "roughly achieves coverage α − (α−1/2)·d/n" regardless of noise distribution.

**Operational plan (n=5 vs n=500 at α=0.1):** fail-closed at n=5 (infinite intervals/No-Bet,
Jackknife+ or SPI substitutes, Venn-Abers for binaries with p₁−p₀>0.20 refusal, Clopper-Pearson
CIs, no public displays below n=30); fully operational split CQR at n=500 (k=451, pinball-loss
quantile nets/GBTs for 0.05/0.95 quantiles, SPCI/rolling-origin for time series, isotonic PAVA
with tie pre-coalescence, Venn-Abers + Platt for binaries, CLV verification, Mondrian subgroup
calibration, Brier/ECE audit gates).

**Known live defect (verified 2026-09-21 in `apps/web/lib/calibration/cqr.ts`):** `conformalQuantile()`
line ~15: `rank = Math.min(Math.max(rank, 0), n - 1);` — clamps the rank to max(n)−1 instead of

## 7. LESSONS — mistakes caught, standards, gotchas

**Task rule (backend-gold):** never bypass logins, paywalls, or access controls; no social
interaction (no likes, follows, replies, reposts, forms). Public-web-only research; every formula
sourced from a primary public source linked inline; anything not found marked GAP rather than invented.

**Neutral-inventory standard (sweeps):** metric name, definition as given, columns/sample values,
date/account, data source as stated, caveats as attributed facts — no verdicts.

**Fake tightness / quantile clamping (the central caught defect):** a small-sample CQR quantile
clamp (`rank = Math.min(Math.max(rank, 0), n - 1)` in `apps/web/lib/calibration/cqr.ts`) was
caught and documented: at n=5, α=0.10 it falsely certifies 90% coverage while delivering 83.33%
(a 6.67pp under-coverage defect), and its tests explicitly encoded the wrong behavior. Standing
rule: ban ALL quantile clamping; emit +∞/No-Bet when n < ⌈1/α⌉−1. Repaired 2026-09-22 per
wiring-plan (`1d38140`) — re-verify against live checkout.

**Name-confusion traps (do NOT conflate):** Barrett's RB Weighted Opportunity (coefficient formula
above, full-PPR) vs. Marvin's WR WOPR (1.5×TS + 0.7×AY%) — different metrics, same name family.
PFF's xFP (2019 article, public formula) vs. FantasyPoints Data Suite current XFP (behind closed
beta — deltas unknown). CQR math must NEVER touch binary moneylines (mathematically invalid for
Y∈{0,1}) — binaries go to Venn-Abers. Closing lines / near-game odds as input features to
team-strength models = severe target leakage (model parrots consensus, CLV unmeasurable).
Average-quality trap: un-conformalized QR under-covers in finite samples (error ∝ d/n) — raw
NN/boosted quantile outputs are strictly *uncalibrated proposal distributions*.

**Jackknife+ reporting honesty:** guarantees 1−2α, NOT 1−α. At α=0.10 → exactly 80% guaranteed
coverage, not 90%. Track/log/report explicitly. The blueprint doc caught itself on this
emphasized correction.

**Venn-Abers threshold arbitrariness:** p₁−p₀ > 0.20 is an example policy value, not a derived
constant — calibrate on shadow data before adopting as a gate. ACI's asymptotic coverage does
NOT certify anything over an 18-week NFL season (no finite-sample guarantee) — don't cite it as
one.

**Data-freshness / update-cadence rules:** NFL stat corrections land Mon–Wed — Thursday's pull
is the cleanest. Raw pbp JSON within ~15 min of game end. Rosters/depth charts/injuries 7 AM UTC
daily. NGS player-level weekly: nightly 3–5 AM ET. nflverse participation: pre-2023 source died
in 2023 season; 2023+ courtesy of FTN, only after all postseason games.

**Small-sample honesty:** uncertainty-aware leg hit rates use Wilson intervals; n=1 splits are
flagged, not headlined. Public performance displays withheld until n ≥ 30 (Clopper-Pearson 95%
CIs). n ≥ 100 settled games before NFL PASS recommendations; n ≥ 1,000 to claim calibration.
"No stats I post are fake, but these ones are 'made up' in the sense that I combined different
stats and sources to improve reliability from a small 1 week sample size" (@acccountstat) — an
explicitly disclosed small-sample blend, the honest pattern vs. fake tightness.

**Model-honesty rules:** per-sport noise scales — a single global calibration layer is
"mathematically unsound" (1701.05976); never share calibration across sports. Train under Brier
loss, not BCE, for calibration (empirical: LSTM+Brier → 0.159 vs Transformer+BCE highest AUC
0.847). Release-time snapshot partitioning for CLV — never train on near-game-time lines. Dual
CLV reporting (Decided 40.8% / System 23.2%) side by side, vs 52.4% break-even floor. Inverted
confidence metrics (Brier 0.3617, z=−10.7) = anti-predictive — purge from any public surface.
Sort by marketFairProb (Shin/Power devigged consensus, Brier 0.2189) until the model
demonstrably beats the close. "Questionable" is a mandated range, not a 50/50 — since 2016.
Rest DNPs (NIR-Rest) are not injury signals. Purge "AI" marketing copy (hygiene governance).
Physical plausibility: player movement >13 m/s = fatally corrupt tel

[part 158] emetry (not an outlier);
wind direction is not naively averaged (store as categorical or directional cosines); non-finite
timestamps = hard error.

**Wiring discipline:** additive-only — new modules + tests, nothing existing touched, nothing
wired into live publish paths (waves 1–2: 454 + 624 implemented, 1,248 + files, zero modified/
deleted). Publish-path wiring (W-1 quantile isotonization, decision modules) = NEEDS HUMAN CALL
with pre-registered acceptance gates. schema.prisma/migrations frozen to agents (law 2); DB reads
forbidden to agents (law 7) — fixture dating fix stays upstream. Prop storage blocked on `PROP`
in Prisma PickType (human schema change). 31 hierarchical-Bayes prop models in
`packages/prediction-engine/src/edge-lab/` wired to quote-plane — storage only blocker.
Training programs (AutoGluon, TimesFM/Chronos/Mamba, LLM fine-tunes, JAGS/Stan weather) are not
small modules — deferred as programs. Hawkes steam detection rejected on short-horizon odds
archives (overfits to high-frequency noise) — replaced by parameter-free RTS Kalman + cubic
B-spline curvature geometry (in the blueprint; the engine's hawkes-steam.ts predates this).
Features W5–W8 (Wasserstein, DFA, Intrinsic Dimension, Permutation Entropy): 12/12 failed →
permanently killed. Mondrian-k calibration ΔCRPS=0.0092 < 0.01 threshold → killed. QB-change
variance scaling τ²=1.379 < 1.50 kill threshold → killed. Spread×Total correlation ρ=0.016 →
independence kept. Hawkes branching ratio n̂=0 → momentum rejected.

**Conversion/extraction gotchas:** equation images dropped by python-docx→markdown (corpus audit's
22 PNGs recovered by rendering; anyone reading only the .md misses the formulas). Table columns
blank in conversion (conformal audit's Exchangeable Y/N and Source ID; Table 2 From/Sender). The

2026-10-08 EPA activation) are 2026-09-19/21 snapshots — re-verify against the live repo before
acting.

**Research-hygiene rules from the audits:** conformal wrappers guarantee coverage but cannot
repair point-estimate bias (fix Brier/ECE of the point model first). Raw boosted/NN quantile
outputs are proposal distributions, not calibrated intervals. Dixon-Coles bivariate Poisson /

decouple-from-consensus thesis (profitability via explicitly decorrelating predictions from
consensus pricing lines). GreerreNFL/nfeloqb URL unverified — verify before citing in public copy.

**E1. Trust no claims, even your own.** Counts must be file-verifiable:
auditable against actual files on disk. When your own count is the
deliverable, the audit reads your files, not your summary. Tracker rows
must reconcile with real files, matching IDs and verdicts, zero
mismatches. (learned 2026-09-21 arXiv audit; expanded in learnings.md)

integrity failure.** The 2026-09-21 arXiv phase-1 rejection: 510 claimed
vs 365 that met the standard; REJECTs must be replaced, never written
off. Garrett rewards honest gaps (they earn bigger mandates) and audits
completion claims. (2026-09-21)

**E3. Never state a contested fact as certain to Garrett.** Greenlaw/Warner
(2026-09-10): carry the conflict, hedge public copy until the primary
source (NFL gamebook) settles it.

**E4. Delete-and-repost on factual errors.** Maye 22/33 → 23/33
(2026-09-10): inaccurate public posts get deleted and corrected, not
edited silently.

**E5. Verify the source of truth before building on it.** SuperGrok
sign-in failure (2026-09-10): the vault username was
signal.origin.hq@gmail.com (Signal Origin's email), not @GalaxySportsHQ's
— a fresh password was rejected because the identity was wrong, not the
credential. Verify handle + account email against the stated target
before publishing to any new surface. (alignment boundary)

**E6. DeepSeek numeric claims are evidence, not verification.** No
execution environment on their side (disclosed 2026-09-13); systemic
citation fabrication found (2026-09-14); quality-gate claims don't match
the scripts they describe. Standing gate: no DeepSeek numeric/discovery
claim is published or built on without Motif-VM execution.

**E7. A fallback render without the material is not a deliverable.**
Faceless-video rejection (2026-09-10) → HARD standing rule (2026-09-15):
if real footage cannot be secured, say so and stop.

**E8. No paywall bypass.** Standing line (2026-09-18, Sports benchmark
lane): public tiers are read-only; gated detail (StatRankings+, PFF Pro,
Data Suite 2.0, paywalled substacks) is not accessed and is documented
as unverified. Leaked public data is usable; research never points past
paywalls.

broadcast.** 2026-09-19 scrub: branches rewritten, all holders told to
reset --hard to the fresh versions before pushing.

**E10. Distinguish snapshots from live state.** Timestamps and statuses in
docs (PR numbers, CI gates, counts, prices, odds lines) are snapshots —
re-check live before any build decision. Memory figures go stale (the
2026-09-24 arXiv-count correction pattern).

**E11. Never publish when the independent model passes.** From the
2026-09-13 calibration audit: the Steelers ML -285 pick shipped even
though the independent model said PASS with -16% edge — codified as the
v5.3.0 regression test.

v5.3.0 build spec (2026-09-13): no claim of completion without executed
evidence. Related: approximate transcriptions (unlabeled scatter axes,
partial visibility, visual estimates) never feed leaderboards — labeled
APPROXIMATE. (learned 2026-09-21 methodology passes)

**E13. Batch handoffs; report gaps first.** When several items need another
agent's input, batch into one handoff (what you did, exact file paths,
what you need, what you're not claiming). Report blockers and partial
progress up front — named gaps beat silent holes. (learned across the
Sept 17-24 sweeps)

**E14. Proactive, not reactive.** Garrett's 2026-09-17 directive: keep
finding benchmark material proactively, not only process charts he sends.
Standing: pursue legal revenue paths autonomously; only true hard blocks

proportional de-vig, `rawEdge = fairProb - impliedProb(avg
chosen-side price)`; edge component `clamp((rawEdge+0.05)/0.10,0,1)*25`;

consensus, depth, edge, volatility, movement, rest, form, data-quality,
H2H, venue, uncertainty, cross-market, schedule-stress, +10 base —
heuristic market-echo composite, NOT calibrated. Signal path: blend
independent home probabilities with sharpness weights |p-0.5|+0.05,
stretch deviations from 0.5 by 1.12 when ≥0.03, confidence = rounded
true probability ×100, edgeScore = max(0, round((trueProb-0.5)*100)).
Gates: confidence ≥70 = PREMIUM; book-path 85/80 Elite, 75/65 Strong,
65/50 Solid, else Lean; signal-path ≥80 Strong, ≥65 Solid, else Lean.

<0.58 consensus; LOW_RISK ≥0.70 consensus with ≥7 books, else MODERATE.

1. **v1.0 CEPT Proposition 1 was ill-posed** (`cept/HONEST_CEPT.md` Remark 4): assumed each

   under performativity. Counterexample: interventions a, b with m(1|do(a))=0.9,
   m(1|do(b))=0.1, p(1|do(b))=0.9; under do(a), E[p(Y|do(b))/m(Y|do(b))] ≈ 8.11 > 1.

2. **The dropped-set Brier integrity check was mathematically vacuous** (Proposition 6):
   for a dropped pick with p = 1/2 + ε, realized score is 1/4 ∓ ε + ε²; dropped picks
   satisfy |ε| < δ, so the dropped set's sample Brier lies in [1/4 − δ(1−δ),
   1/4 + δ(1+δ)] **for every possible outcome sequence** — pinned near 0.25
   deterministically by the selection rule. It cannot work. Replacement: run the
   skill-vs-market e-process and calibration instruments on the dropped set. The
   blindness cuts the direction that matters: dropped picks with p=0.5, true q=0.7,
   market m=0.4 beat the market at a compounding e-process log-rate of ≈0.10
   nats/pick while scoring exactly 0.25 — real, discarded edge the check passes.

# PART 2 — Standards established

1. **Trust no claims, even your own.** Counts must be file-verifiable — auditable
   against actual files on disk. Tracker rows reconcile with real files, matching IDs
   and verdicts, zero mismatches. (learned 2026-09-21 arXiv audit; memory-sports-
   learnings.md §E1)
2. **Framing a

[part 178] phase "done" without the standard being met is the integrity failure.**
   (2026-09-21; memory-sports-learnings.md §E2)
3. **Every number carries league context** — rank, percentile, or average line, or it
   is cut. (edge-sheet design brief; pre-sept17-digest.md)
4. **Every proprietary metric gets a birth certificate** — source-rights envelope,
   payload-rights classification, metric card, model card, validation report, drift
   card, public/private exposure level — before promotion. (R&D map § Source rights)
5. **The Evidence Readiness Matrix** — factors ACTIVE / SHADOW_READY / SHADOW_COLLECTING
   / BLOCKED / ABSENT; scoring reads only ACTIVE factors; true EV stays blocked until
   independent fair probability is source-backed and separately promoted. (2026-05-21)
6. **Shadow-first, then product**: every method becomes a deterministic, tested,
   documented shadow primitive before influencing public claims; CEPT instruments run in
   shadow; the learning loop's champion/challenger and shadow deployment are the
   reference. (R&D map; ML brief §15)
7. **Pre-registered hypotheses with kill lines**: anything entering the engine carries a
   pre-registered hypothesis with a kill line written on the same line as the
   prediction, a shared test set, fixture-grouped time-ordered folds, a result recorded
   whether it lives or dies. (ML brief; props-consensus H1/H2/H3)
8. **Absent = factor does not fire**: missing data is ABSENT, never zero — factor
   engine convention; the `consensus` factor: NEVER fabricate — absent = the factor
   does not fire.
9. **Never collapse skill/profit/self-honesty into one number** (CEPT §4); never
   overstate — implemented-and-running-in-shadow-mode, validation-pending is the
   correct statement until the validation procedure's step 4.
10. **Cite or don't claim**: every legal proposition gets primary-source support;
    unverifiable citations marked UNVERIFIED rather than presented as established.
11. **Denominators, filters, sample windows, and minimum qualifiers are first-class
    fields** (e.g., true target share = % of **team pass attempts**, not targets;
    Statyx "last_3" = NQ = not qualified). (sept18-digest.md)
12. **Approximate chart transcriptions stay approximate** — never promoted to canonical
    values. Chart-reads are approximate; formulas are exact. Author-stated formulas
    (ARBY's footer, ThunderDan's 80/20 blend, benbbaldwin's 40/40/20) are the
    reverse-engineering-grade material. (sept18-digest.md; sept19-24-digest.md)
13. **Distinct denominators mean distinct metrics** — success-rate conventions don't
    merge across sources; reposts and new cuts of existing metrics are revisits, not
    new metrics. (sept18-digest.md)
14. **Neutral-inventory standard**: metric name, definition as given, columns/sample
    values, date/account, data source as stated, caveats as attributed facts — no
    verdicts. (sept21-deep-digest.md)
15. **Evaluation discipline**: choose δ on an early chronological window, evaluate on a
    later one — a threshold tuned and scored on the same rows is a curve fit (CEPT);
    report π_δ on the held-out window; report effect sizes with sample sizes and proper
    time-ordered splits; report negative results. (ML brief)
16. **The ML-regime reminder**: evaluate every method against low SNR (edges worth
    having are 1–3 percentage points), an efficient price, small uneven samples,

2. **Decision doctrine**: confidence is not win probability; GSE Signal Score is
   decision quality, not win probability; no bet is a decision; high EV cannot override
   missing data, stale inputs, unclear rights, drift, or calibration debt.

   no CLV success claims without sample size and approval; any accuracy-theater
   without floors is a brand anti-pattern. (R&D map; prediction-market triage)

   resale; no raw sports data resale; never re-serve raw restricted feeds as the
   product; raw NGS *row* exposure banned. Raw paid odds payloads exposed only where
   terms allow.

   misuse, fake accounts; check `source-rights-registry.ts` before scraping a fantasy
   site; never put a real book's quotes into a paid SaaS without rights.
   (scrape-wave-2)

   copy-trade, no whale-alert customer features, no guaranteed-edge claims.

   phrasing in public copy; no hashtag walls; human voice; team names FULL CAPS when
   large; BUF/DET only inside chart legends and data labels; sharp-friend test for

   this?" Every public number traces to a source; every claim can be verified; show

# PART 4 — Gotchas and transcription hazards

1. **OddsPapi traps** (vendor-documented): `hasOdds=false` on finished fixtures is
   expected, not missing data; identical price tuples must be grouped empirically
   (`cloneOf` doesn't track all duplicates); tournamentId lifts the 10-day fixture
   window; historical-odds retention disputed (docs say Jan 2026, independent probe
   ~90 days) — resolve live before backfill; "free" endpoints still 429 after plan
   exhaustion. Key hygiene: OddsPapi key is a query param — never log the query
   string; 429 body carries `error.retryMs` as valid JSON — honor it.
2. **Close semantics**: no `is_closing` field — close = last active snapshot with
   `createdAt < kickoff`; Pinnacle prices in-play so a pre-KO cutoff is mandatory.
3. **Pinnacle `limit`** per snapshot = max stake = a confidence signal no other free
   source carries — persist it.
4. **persist `externalProviders`** at fixture ingest — collapses entity resolution
   across every downstream feed keyed to any listed provider.
5. **ESPN public endpoints**: undocumented, unstable; UA behavior changes responses
   (403 browser UA vs 200 plain curl).
6. **Do not retry**: rbsdm.com (failed to load in mission), statrankings provider
   inference from FTN/Kevin Adams link, fantasy-points paywalled articles.
7. **Manual charting QA** (from b_peters12 recon): store observed geometry separately
   from inferred team terminology; double-chart, adjudicate, compute inter-rater
   reliability, retain timestamped film evidence, version the codebook.
8. **Under-center cut**: needs explicit treatment of no-plays, spikes, kneels,
   penalties, pistol; exact nflverse field names unverified.
9. **StatRankings JS inventory** (`statrankings/js/`): 103 files; controllers reveal app
   features — stat builder, projection overrides, survivor grid, implied probability,
   market search, depth-chart overrides, coverage shell controllers, paywall modal,
   PDF export. Controller names = UI capabilities evidence, **not public API endpoints**.
   `nfl-urls.txt` = 1,148 paths; `methodology-definitions.json` = 673 glossary
   definitions (prose, no proprietary formulas — ARBY/Havoc/PROE+/xFP definitions
   absent).
10. **Composite-metric construction patterns observed in the wild**: ARBY (65% ARBY /
    35% RB YPC, 65% prior-year / 35% current-year, 50/50 offense-defense; TNF version
    adds game-weighting 5/2 across windows); benbbaldwin pass-protection composite (PFF
    40% / SIS blown-block 40% / ESPN PBWR 20%, each source re-scaled 0–100 before
    blending); SamHoppen Week 3 composite power ratings (mean of 6 sources as expected
    spread vs. average, per-team std dev as the disagreement measure); ThunderDan PROJ
    YPPR (prior-year baseline × projected opponent coverage splits, 80/20 old/new
    blend); RaritosFootball Nota (EPA + success rate + pressure → 1–10 with
    attack/defense sub-ratings). When reverse-engineering a public composite, look for
    this shape: weighted blend of public/paid inputs + a prior-year anchor + a
    normalization step.
11. **Most of the signal is vendor-gated; the construction is what matters.** The
    valuable reverse-engineering targets are the open methodology + construction
    patterns, not the charted data (FTN, PFF, Statyx, SIS, ESPN PBWR are all gated).
12. **Same-caveat explosive-play counts** (@DETROlTLions313, Sep 23): the Claude-built
    query excluded QB runs — Seattle's allowed 10+ rushes read 2 in the dashboard vs 4
    manually counted (Drake Maye 16 and 10, Stevenson 12, Bam Knight 18). Any
    explosive-rush pipeline mus

[part 182] t explicitly include or exclude QB runs and say which;
    verify against other sources before comparing. **Position-aware baselines**:
    WillBrinson's caveat on the rushing-EPA chart — QB rushing (scrambles, situational
    runs) is not comparable to traditional RB rushing; keep position-aware reference
    lines. **nflverse pbp has no alignment data**: slot/X/Y/Z attribution needs
    charting data (FTN/PFF/Statyx).
13. **The no-code pipeline recipe is engine-replicable** (@DETROlTLions313): natural-
    language prompt → Claude → RStudio + nflreadr → BigQuery → Grafana. End-to-end
    verified by a third party. Cumulative EPA by play number (not by week) is a trend
    shape the engine can mirror for any quarterback.
14. **DeepSeek numeric claims are evidence, not verification** (no execution
    environment on their side; disclosed 2026-09-13). Standing gate: no DeepSeek
    numeric/discovery claim is published or built on without Motif-VM execution.
15. **Never publish when the independent model passes** (2026-09-13 calibration audit:
    the Steelers ML -285 pick shipped even though the independent model said PASS with
    −16% edge — codified as the v5.3.0 regression test). Related: verify the source of
    truth before building on it (2026-09-10 SuperGrok identity mismatch: wrong email =
    wrong identity, not bad credential).
16. **The 2026-09-24 arXiv-count "correction" pattern**: a subagent's claimed count is
    a lead, not a fact — needs Motif-level verification before promoting to the
    record. (memory-sports-learnings.md §E24, §C)
17. **Browser-harness daemon wedge** (jev-ultrafast, 2026-09-24): if CDP calls time

### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)
- @MagicSportsGuy's ARBY RB Matchup Rating: new composite kernel blending a run-blocking metric (65% ARBY) with RB efficiency (35% RB yards per carry, no QB/WR/TE runs), seasons (65% 2025 / 35% 2026-to-date), and sides of the ball (50/50 offense-defense) into one matchup score — a twist on Adjusted-Line-Yards-style metrics.
- Run Type Matchup (statyxio): twist on the inventoried Rush IQ package — crosses the runner's own concept split (Inside Zone / Outside Zone / Gap %) with the opponent's per-concept YPC-allowed rank and a Softer/Tougher tag; composite usage-share × defensive-strength by scheme concept.
- Target Area Matchup grid (statyxio): twist — target share + REC/G by 12 field-area cells crossed with a per-cell defensive rank ("Rank 1 is the strongest defense"; Tough/Average/Soft/Nq). Combines the player's area-target map with the defense's area toughness.
- Mayfield CPOE-vs-EPA split (statyxio): accuracy (CPOE +14.0, 3rd of 32) juxtaposed with efficiency (EPA/dropback −0.223, 28th) as an explicit diagnostic ("Accuracy and efficiency are telling two different stories"), framed against the opponent's EPA allowed and the QB's deep-throw rate (3.7%). A contrast-based QB evaluation framing, not a new formula.
- "Mapped carries"/"mapped work" (statyxio: Jeanty 23 mapped carries, Likely "mapped work") — run-lane/concept mapping of every carry (e.g. "48% through the middle") as the unit of analysis rather than raw carries; the underlying primitive behind the rush board.

1. **@csv_enjoyer (Ray Carpenter).** The open-data well. His research is reproducible by design — EPA/play, success rate, rush-gap splits and Bayesian ranking work you can actually audit and rebuild from. For any engine project, he is the single best source of public methods to benchmark against.

# Method Deep-Dives: 10 Engagement Targets

## 1. Ray Carpenter — @csv_enjoyer

**Computational method.** Carpenter's contribution is data-engineering infrastructure, not a predictive model: he builds reproducible NFL analytics pipelines with a modern stack — Docker, dbt, Airflow, Kubernetes, DuckDB — over raw nflfastR CSVs. His public repo `football_data_engineering` implements a bronze → silver → gold medallion architecture: bronze = raw CSV from nflfastR; silver = cleaned team abbreviations (dbt views/tables); gold = aggregated stats; plus dbt data-quality tests and Airflow DAGs for orchestration. Quick start: `python download.py 2025`, then `dbt run`, `dbt test`.
**Inputs/rules.** Raw nflfastR play-by-play CSVs; dbt models for staging/cleaning; k8s manifests; Airflow DAGs. No betting rules — the "model" is the pipeline itself.
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** GitHub repo `array-carpenter/football_data_engineering` (active; updated ~104 days before Sept 2026 crawl). Authorship line in the repo README: "Ray Carpenter — @csv_enjoyer | thespade.substack.coom". Substack: The Spade (thespade.substack.com).
**Data sources.** nflfastR (nflverse) raw CSVs; DuckDB as the compute layer.
**Differentiator.** He treats NFL analytics as a *data-engineering* problem first — most of the ecosystem argues about models while running ad-hoc notebooks; Carpenter's edge is production-grade pipelines (dbt tests, Airflow scheduling, Kubernetes) that make analysis repeatable. Engagement angle: pipeline reliability, dbt modeling patterns, nflverse data-quality issues.
**Evidence:** https://github.com/array-carpenter/football_data_engineering

## 2. Ben Baldwin — @benbbaldwin

**Computational method.** Baldwin is the co-founder of the RBSDM.com database and the **nflfastR** R package (efficient access to NFL play-by-play data with EPA/WP columns baked in), and author/maintainer of **nfl4th** — an R package (CRAN, v1.0.4, MIT) of functions to calculate *optimal fourth-down decisions*. nfl4th imports xgboost, mgcv, nflfastR, and nflreadr, and powers the **@ben_bot_baldwin** 4th-down decision bot, which grades every coach's go-for-it/kick/punt call in near real time against the model's recommendation.
**Inputs/rules.** nflfastR play-by-play; expected-points and win-probability models underneath; the bot's decision rule is "go when the model's win-probability-maximizing recommendation says go." Public track record: using his code and data, theScore found teams went for it in toss-up situations 16.8% (2019) → 18.1% (2020) → 26.5% (early 2021) — the league moved *toward* the model.
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** jetsxfactor.com (Feb 20, 2023) quotes his canonical line: "No team should ever punt on 4th & 3 in a game they are losing." theScore (Sept 2021) on the bot's league-wide influence. CRAN nfl4th docs (published 2023-08-21).

## 3. Aaron Schatz — @ASchatzNFL

**Computational method.

[part 288] ** Creator of **DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average)**, now housed at FTN Fantasy. Method: every NFL play is compared to a league-average baseline *for that exact situation* — down, distance, field position. Five yards on 3rd-and-4 is worth far more than five yards on 3rd-and-12. Opponent adjustments are applied (passing also adjusted by target position group: RB/TE/WR), fourth-quarter blowout performance is downweighted, all fumbles count equally, and each season is normalized so league average = 0%. Weighted DVOA decays early-season games. The preseason **projection system** (2026 edition, Sept 2026): offense/defense/special-teams DVOA projected separately via regressions trained on 2012–2024 data; inputs = three-year DVOA + separate QB projection + regression-to-mean adjustments (personnel changes, coaching experience, draft history, OL age/tenure, returning-from-injury players); QBs new to a system are penalized unless elite. The 32 team projections run through **50,000 season simulations** with a dynamic adjustment (+1.5% DVOA to winners, −1.5% to losers within a sim) to mimic in-season learning.
**Inputs/rules.** NFL play-by-play (straight from the league — Schatz has explicitly corrected the record that DVOA is *not* charting-based); preseason priors; 50k Monte Carlo sims.
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** *FTN Football Almanac 2026* (21st annual edition, July 2025 lineage); "Aaron Schatz's 2026 DVOA Projections" (ftnfantasy.com, Sept 2026); FTN DVOA rankings/method page (opponent adjustments begin after Week 4; Forest Index for Estimated Wins).
**Data sources.** NFL official play-by-play; FTN charting for adjacent products.
**Differentiator.** DVOA is the longest-running opponent- and situation-adjusted efficiency system in football (roots in *The Hidden Game of Football*), and Schatz's projection write-ups are unusually honest about their own weird outputs ("A few of them will look strange to you. A few of them look strange to *me*.").
**Evidence:** https://ftnfantasy.com/nfl/aaron-schatzs-2026-dvoa-projections · http://ftnfantasy.com/stats/nfl/team-total-dvoa

## 6. Seth Walder — @SethWalder

**Computational method.** ESPN analytics writer (since 2017) and ESPN Bet Live regular. His analytical home base is ESPN's **Football Power Index (FPI)**: a Bayesian predictive rating measuring points better/worse than an average NFL team on a neutral field. EPA is the foundation — each play gets an adjusted EPA from historical data, decomposed into offensive, defensive, and special-teams components. Preseason priors sit on unit EPA rates derived from preseason expectations; the *only* single position that moves FPI is quarterback (predictive QBR added, with aging curves, injury probability, and replacement-level rookies). Game-level projections add altitude, travel distance (~0.5 pts in extremes), rest differentials, and seasonal offensive-EPA decay; each team's season is then simulated **10,000 times** for playoff/Super Bowl/draft-slot odds. Walder's own framing (quoted 2023): FPI rankings are "based substantially on win totals from Caesars Sportsbook and strength of schedule, along with factors such as past team performance and returning starters" — i.e., the model is deliberately market-aware.
**Inputs/rules.** EPA per play by unit; QB efficiency/injury probability; travel/rest/altitude; market win totals as a prior input; 10k Monte Carlo season sims.
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** "Biggest NFL Football Power Index swings of the season" (ESPN, Nov 13, 2021 — byline confirms analytics-writer role and @SethWalder handle); Wharton Moneyball clip on real-time probability tools; ESPN's "Guide to NFL FPI."
**Data sources.** NFL play-by-play; ESPN Stats & Info; Caesars win totals; QBR components.
**Differentiator.** Walder is the public explainer-in-chief for the most-cited black-box-adjacent model in mainstream football media — and he's unusually candid that FPI *leans on the betting market* as an input, which is exactly the market-vs-model tension GSE should engage him on.
**Evidence:** https://www.espn.ph/nfl/insider/story/_/id/32608631/biggest-nfl-football-power-index-swings-season-which-teams-better-worse-preseason-expectations · https://www.espn.ph/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/123048/a-guide-to-nfl-fpi

## 7. Kevin Cole — @KevinCole___

**Computational method.** Creator of **Unexpected Points** (ex-PFF). Three signature methods: (1) **Adjusted scores** — weekly "advanced reviews" that quantify team play quality by emphasizing stable metrics (success rate, adjusted EPA) and downweighting high-variance events (turnovers, special teams, penalties, fumble luck); tested against actual scores for slight predictive lift. (2) **Bayesian Quarterback Rankings** — go-forward projections of adjusted QB efficiency, blending multi-season adjusted EPA/play priors (250-dropback minimums) with current-season evidence. (3) **Improvement Index** — projects a team's upcoming season from the prior year's roster, then adjusts for offseason changes with an NBA-style plus-minus: player value measured by EPA-based on/off-field impact, smoothed through clustering of similar players, weighted by participation (snap counts), with injury-risk, coordinator-change, and scheme-tendency adjustments. A +43 index means ~43 points of point-differential improvement vs. keeping the roster intact (~1.3 wins).
**Inputs/rules.** Play-by-play EPA and success rate; snap counts; roster/coordinator changes; DraftKings Showdown slate sims (methodology + most-similar-historical-matchup comps per slate).
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** Weekly "Advanced Reviews" and "Bayesian Quarterback Rankings" (Unexpected Points, 2024–2025 seasons); "The QB G

**Data sources.** nflverse-style play-by-play; PFF grades (as a cross-check against EPA, not an input — Cole notes where they align/diverge); historical rosters.
**Differentiator.** Cole is the rare analyst whose weekly product is *explicitly* built on the stable-vs-noisy decomposition — he publishes the adjusted score alongside the real one every week, so his process is auditable in public.

## 8. Warren Sharp — @SharpFootball

**Computational method.** Sharp Football Analysis is built on situational efficiency decomposition: **EPA per play, success rate, and explosive-play rate (15+ yard gains)**, sliced by down, quarter, score state, personnel, box count, and play-action usage. Signature moves: (a) early-down efficiency isolated from garbage time (first-half, first-three-quarters splits); (b) box-count analysis — e.g., ranking a run defense specifically against light boxes (6-man) vs. stacked boxes; (c) play-action usage-vs-efficiency gaps (a team at 22% PA usage when league average is 33% despite +0.22 EPA/att with PA); (d) explosive pass *defense* schedule adjustments (a QB's explosiveness re-weighted by the schedule of explosive-pass defenses faced); (e) the "first half matters more than the second half" thesis — halftime leads force opponents predictable, and predictability is the one thing that gives defenses the edge back. Annual 350–400-page *Sharp Football Preview* with team-by-team chapters.
**Inputs/rules.** Play-by-play with personnel/box-count/play-action charting; early-down and first-half filters; schedule-strength adjustments for explosiveness.
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** "The Formula to Attack the Ravens Defense" (sharpfootballanalysis.com — light-box splits); "8 NFL Offenses That Could Be More Explosive in 2023"; 2018 Eagles preview (explosive-pass-defense scheduling); Awful Announcing interview (method philosophy: first-half leverage, predictability).
**Data sources.** Licensed play-by-play/charting data (Sharp's operation charts its own splits); sportsbook futures for the preview's expectations framing.
**Differentiator.** Sharp's unit of analysis is the *coaching tendency*, not the player — his content reads like a scouting report on play-callers, which is why his "why did they lose" postmortems (coaching? injuries? turnovers? first-down play-calling?) travel so well with both bettors and fantasy players.
**Evidence:** https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/analysis/ravens-defense-how-to-attack-warren-sharp/amp/ · https://awfulannouncing.com/nfl/football-analytics-expert-warren-sharp-interview.html?wComments=1

## 9. Rufus Peabody — @RufusPeabody

**Computational method.** Professional bettor and Unabated co-founder; operates as an **originator** — his computer models generate their own numbers on hundreds of markets (notably props), and his team's action *moves* the lines everyone else reacts to. Core philosophy, stated in his own words: "relying on the process that generates outcomes rather than the outcomes themselves." Concretely: fumble recoveries are random (no predictive skill) — if the market doesn't discount fumble-recovery luck, it overvalues lucky teams; garbage-time performance is discounted; recent performance is downweighted (most people overweight recency); weather and opponent strength are controlled for. He describes his model as a **bias-index**: if the market says Team A −7 and his model says −3, the true number is expected near −5.2 — and he only bets when the disparity clears the rake, sizing up with the edge. Early-career signature: betting MLB/NFL **totals** with models incorporating **barometric pressure and humidity**. On props: mostly unders (public loves overs), bet early for overs, as late as possible for unders.
**Inputs/rules.** Raw play-by-play + situational charting (defenders at the line of scrimmage, DB counts); weather data; market lines as the comparison baseline; Kelly-style sizing (implied by disparity-scaled bets — exact staking formula UNVERIFIED, never published).
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** RotoWire "Beating the Book: Q&A with Rufus Peabody" (bias-index explanation); The Ringer's "The King of Super Bowl Props" two-parter (Sept 2022 — originator operation, international betting team

[part 291] s); bookies.com interview ("You're using your intuition to sort of think logically about it and come up with a framework... it's just an estimate"); Wharton Moneyball on prediction markets vs. sportsbooks (2026); co-host of the @BetTheProcess podcast.
**Data sources.** Licensed play-by-play; weather feeds; sportsbook APIs/odds screens.
**Differentiator.** Peabody is one of the only public figures who *is the market-maker's problem* — his edge isn't a published metric but a private model stack whose outputs are validated by the only scoreboard that matters (closing-line value and profit). His "bias-index" framing is the cleanest articulation anywhere of how a model should be used *against* a market rather than as a ranking.
**Evidence:** https://www.rotowire.com/football/article.php?id=40172 · https://www.theringer.com/2022/09/21/gambling/gamblers-super-bowl-props-rufus-peabody-nfl

## 10. Robby Greer — @greerreNFL

**Computational method.** Author of **nfelo** (nfeloapp.com) — "a power ranking, prediction, and betting model for the NFL" that takes FiveThirtyEight's Elo framework and adapts it for the NFL. Components: (1) **nfelo** — main team Elo with HFA, rest-day, and weather adjustments, explicitly **regressed toward market spreads** to improve margin prediction; (2) **nfeloqb** — separate QB Elo, replicating and improving 538's QB model; (3) **nfelosrs** — SRS approach for market-implied team strength from win-total futures. Newer **nfelounits** package decomposes team performance into measurable unit ratings (passing, rushing, special teams) using EPA from play-by-play, translated to Elo: an EWMA (exponentially weighted moving average) tracks unit performance with offseason regression and contextual game adjustments; unit ratings = predicted point differential vs. an average team; an EloTranslator combines units into a single Elo trained to minimize log-loss on game win probability. Outputs: power rankings, per-game spreads, win probabilities, EV vs. market lines, full-season sims. Distribution: free site + auto-updated CSVs on GitHub + pip package (`nfelodcm`); tracked publicly on PredictionTracker.
**Inputs/rules.** Game scores and margins (Elo updates); QB identities (QB Elo); market spreads/win totals (regression targets); EPA by unit (nfelounits); weather/rest/HFA adjustments.
**Dated threads/papers/posts.** GitHub repos `greerreNFL/nfelo` (v4.00 rebuild) and `greerreNFL/nfelounits`; nfeloapp.com weekly predictions; nfeloqb update cadence (Tue/Thu mornings in-season per repo docs).
**Data sources.** Historical game results; betting-market lines; nflverse play-by-play for EPA inputs.
**Differentiator.** The most *transparent* Elo-based betting model in public: open-source code, published CSVs, pip-installable, third-party tracked. And the most honest about its own epistemology — regressing to the market is disclosed, not hidden, making it a clean "market + model blend" benchmark for GSE's engine.
**Evidence:** https://github.com/greerreNFL/nfelo · https://github.com/greerreNFL/nfelounits

## 1. Expected points (EP)

### Key sources

- **Yurko, Ventura & Horowitz, "nflWAR: A Reproducible Method for Offensive Player Evaluation in Football"** (arXiv 1802.00998, 2018) — primary paper. Full text read: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1802.00998v1
- **Brill, Yee, Deshpande & Wyner, "Moving from Machine Learning to Statistics: the case of Expected Points in American football"** (arXiv 2409.04889, 2024) — primary critique: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04889
- **nflfastR R-package docs (CRAN)** — current production EP interface: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nflfastR/nflfastR.pdf
- **fastrmodels R-package docs (CRAN)** — current model objects: https://ftp.openbsd.dk/pub/mirrors/pub/cran/web/packages/fastrmodels/fastrmodels.pdf

### Method summary (Yurko et al., the reproducible foundation)

EP is estimated as the expected value of the **next scoring event within the same half**, modeled directly as a **multinomial logistic regression** over seven outcome categories from the possession team's perspective: touchdown (+7), field goal (+3), safety (+2), no score (0), opponent safety (−2), opponent field goal (−3), opponent touchdown (−7). Six logits are fit relative to a "no score" baseline; EP is then the probability-weighted sum of the seven point values. The response is classification, not regression, because the point-value gaps between events violate linear-regression residual assumptions. Covariates are just six: down (1–4), seconds remaining in half, yardline, log(yards to go), goal-to-go indicator, under-two-minutes indicator — plus three interactions (log(YTG)×down, yardline×down, log(YTG)×goal-to-go). Two methodological choices matter: (1) **observation weighting** — plays are down-weighted by score differential and by "drives until the next score," because blowout plays and distant-future scores distort the fit; (2) **model selection by calibration, not likelihood** — predicted probabilities are binned in 5% increments against observed event rates and the model with the best leave-one-season-out (LOSO) calibration error is chosen (final e ≈ 0.013). Kick plays get special overrides: two-point attempts use a flat 47.35% historical rate (0.947 EP); extra points and field goals use a generalized additive model of make-probability as a smooth function of kick distance only, with a missed-FG correction of 8 yards field position and 5.07 seconds.

### What changed since

Current nflfastR's production `ep_model` is a serialized **XGBoost** model (confirmed in fastrmodels CRAN docs), and its EP function returns the full seven-event probability vector (p_no_score, p_opp_fg, p_opp_safety, p_opp_td, p_fg, p_safety, p_td) plus the aggregated EP. Yurko's multinomial logistic regression is the reproducible foundation; it is **not** what current nflfastR runs. Brill et al. (2024) further warn that play-level EP models inherit drive-level dependence (many plays share one eventual score), selection bias, and overfitting artifacts, and lack uncertainty estimates.

### Implementation takeaway for the engine

Implement EP as a two-stage **event-probability → weighted-sum** model (the probability vector is the valuable artifact — it feeds win probability and fourth-down models too). If starting simple, Yurko's six-covariate multinomial logit is fully reproducible from the paper; upgrade t

[part 297] o gradient boosting only after the simple version is calibrated. **Validate with LOSO or drive-clustered splits, never random play splits** — multiple plays on the same drive share the same eventual scoring event, so random play-level splits leak the label. Weight or filter blowout and far-from-score observations the way Yurko does.

### Verification status

- VERIFIED (primary, full text): Yurko EP = multinomial logistic regression, seven scoring events, covariates + interactions + observation weighting + LOSO calibration selection.
- VERIFIED (primary docs): current nflfastR/fastrmodels `ep_model` is XGBoost, returns the seven-event probability vector.
- VERIFIED (primary, abstract/search text): Brill et al. 2024 critiques drive-level dependence, selection bias, overfitting, missing uncertainty.
- UNVERIFIED: the exact feature set, training window, and hyperparameters of the current XGBoost EP model — the two methodology pages I located (Open Source Football 2020 nflfastR model article and its Wayback copy) both failed to load and were not retried. Do not claim to know nflfastR's current feature list.

## 2. CPOE (completion percentage over expected)

### Key sources

- **nflfastR R-package docs (CRAN)** — defines `cp` (completion probability) and `cpoe`: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nflfastR/nflfastR.pdf
- **fastrmodels R-package docs (CRAN)** — current `cp_model` object class: https://ftp.openbsd.dk/pub/mirrors/pub/cran/web/packages/fastrmodels/fastrmodels.pdf
- nflfastR's original CP-model methodology article (Open Source Football, 2020-09-28) — **located but could not be fetched; Wayback copy also failed. Not retried. Treated as unavailable.**

### Method summary

CPOE is a residual: for each pass attempt, a completion-probability model produces `cp` (probability the pass is completed given context), and play-level `cpoe = complete_pass − cp` (1 if completed, 0 if not, minus predicted probability). Aggregation to player/team level is the mean residual over attempts. That is the entire public definition — CPOE is model-agnostic; its quality equals the quality of the underlying `cp` model. What I could verify about the current public implementation: nflfastR's `cp_model` in fastrmodels is a serialized **XGBoost** model, not a logistic regression.

### Implementation takeaway for the engine

CPOE belongs in the engine as a **QB/team passing-efficiency feature** that is opponent- and situation-adjusted by construction (the `cp` model conditions on context). Use team-level rolling mean CPOE as an input to the Elo adjustment or as a spread/moneyline feature; never aggregate raw completion percentage. Because play-level CPOE is a Bernoulli residual, season aggregates need **shrinkage toward zero for low attempt counts** (early season, backup QBs).

### Verification status

- VERIFIED (primary docs): `cp` = completion probability; play-level `cpoe = complete_pass − cp`; aggregation = mean residual; current `cp_model` is XGBoost.
- UNVERIFIED: the exact feature set (throw depth, receiver separation, pressure, etc.), training window, and validation of nflfastR's current `cp_model`. The original methodology article failed to load twice and was not retried.
- UNVERIFIED (attribution): the "logistic model using throw depth, receiver separation, pressure" description could **not** be tied to nflfastR from any source I read. Those features match tracking-based (Next Gen Stats-style) expected-completion models, not necessarily nflfastR's public play-by-play model. Do not present that feature list as nflfastR's.

## 3. DVOA / DAVE

### Key sources

- **FTN Fantasy, "Week 1 DVOA: San Francisco's Big Victory" (Aaron Schatz, 2026)** — current method details: https://ftnfantasy.com/nfl/week-1-dvoa-san-franciscos-big-victory
- **FTN Fantasy, "Aaron Schatz's 2026 DVOA Projections" (2026)** — preseason forecast inputs: https://ftnfantasy.com/nfl/aaron-schatzs-2026-dvoa-projections
- **FTN Fantasy, "Week 11 DVOA: 49ers Now on Top" (2025)** — early-season DAVE blend weights: https://ftnfantasy.com/nfl/week-11-dvoa-49ers-now-on-top
- Historical origin: Schatz, *Pro Football Prospectus* (Football Outsiders). No peer-reviewed paper found; the provider's own writing is the primary source.

### Method summary

**DVOA** (defense-adjusted value over average) compares **every play to a situational league-average baseline** for that down, distance, and field position, and explicitly values **progress toward a first down rath

[part 298] er than raw yards** (a 3-yard gain on 3rd-and-2 beats an 8-yard gain on 3rd-and-10). Each play is then adjusted for the quality of the opponent faced — the defining step that makes DVOA an opponent-adjusted efficiency metric rather than a raw one. Verified current details (Schatz, 2026): early-season opponent adjustments use **prior-year information** (Week 1 2026 used 50% of the prior year's opposing pass-offense adjustment, 30% run offense, 20% opposing defense); and DVOA treats **all fumbles the same whether recovered or not**, directly baking fumble-recovery randomness into the metric. **DAVE** (DVOA adjusted for variation early) blends the preseason projection with observed DVOA, with the blend shifting as the season accumulates: after Week 1 of 2026, DAVE was **83% preseason forecast for offense and 98% preseason for defense/special teams** (Week 11 of 2025: 12% forecast for offense, 35% for defense) — a shrinkage scheme that trusts small-sample offensive data earlier than defensive data. The 2026 preseason forecasts combine three prior seasons of DVOA, a separate starting-QB projection, regression to the mean, personnel changes, coaching experience, draft history, offensive-line age/tenure, and injuries.

### Implementation takeaway for the engine

DVOA is the template for the engine's **opponent-adjusted efficiency layer**: per-play value over a situational baseline, opponent-adjusted, with fumble luck stripped out by counting all fumbles equally. Since the exact DVOA formula is proprietary, implement a **DVOA-inspired** metric: EPA per play adjusted for opponent (iterative or regression-based strength-of-schedule correction), regressed early-season with a DAVE-style preseason-prior blend (heavier prior on defense, which stabilizes slower). The Week-1 50/30/20 prior-year opponent-adjustment split is a concrete, citable starting point for early-season games.

### Verification status

- VERIFIED (provider, 2026): play-vs-situational-baseline construction, first-down-progress weighting, opponent adjustments, all-fumbles-equal treatment, DAVE blend definition and exact 2026 Week-1 weights (83%/98%), preseason forecast input list, early-season prior-year opponent-adjustment splits (50/30/20).
- UNVERIFIED: the exact per-play DVOA weights, the full opponent-adjustment formula, and the precise DAVE decay schedule. These are proprietary; any engine implementation is "DVOA-inspired," never "DVOA."
- UNVERIFIED: no peer-reviewed publication of the DVOA method was located; Schatz's provider writing is the best primary source.

## 4. Fourth-down win probability (nfl4th)

### Key sources

- **nfl4th R package, official site** — `add_4th_probs` model documentation (go/punt/FG submodels, outputs, stated limitations): https://www.nfl4th.com/
- **nfl4th CRAN manual (2026)** — function reference: https://cran.asia/web/packages/nfl4th/nfl4th.pdf
- **Sandholtz, Wu, Puterman & Chan, "Learning Risk Preferences in Markov Decision Processes: an Application to the Fourth Down Decision in the NFL"** (arXiv 2309.00756v2, 2024) — academic treatment, confirms nfl4th's WP model as the decision engine and surveys the literature: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.00756v2
- Lineage: Romer (2006, dynamic programming — coaches far too conservative); Burke et al. (2014, 4th Down Calculator); Baldwin (2021a, fourth-down decision bot); Yam & Lopez (2019, conservative decisions cost ~0.4 wins/year); Daly-Grafstein (2023, selection-bias correction via Heckman model); Lopez (2020, yardage-rounding confounding inflates aggressiveness); Brill, Yurko & Wyner (2023, uncertainty understated in WP-based policies); Roach & Owens (2024, coaches overweight recent failures).

### Method summary

The nfl4th decision engine is **expected win probability, compared across actions**: for a given fourth-down state it estimates WP(go), WP(field goal), and WP(punt) and recommends the action with the highest expected WP; the reported "go boost" is the WP advantage of going over the best kick/punt alternative. The three action models are separate components (documented on nfl4th.com): the **go model** predicts a full distribution of yards gained and includes first downs awarded by defensive penalty; the **punt model** includes blocks, return touchdowns, and fumbled returns; the **FG model** is kick-make probability as a function of distance and roof type. These feed a win-probability model — Sandholtz et al. confirm the package's WP estimates come from the nflfastR-fami

[part 299] ly WP model (Baldwin 2024) — with game-state inputs including yardline, yards to go, score differential, time remaining, and timeouts. Stated limitations (official site): the go model **excludes turnover returns**; the punt model ignores player identity and some penalties; the FG model ignores kicker identity, outdoor weather, and blocked-return outcomes. The academic literature adds three corrections an engine should respect: raw-data estimates are corrupted by **selection bias** (only good teams attempt aggressive 4ths — correct with a Heckman-style selection model per Daly-Grafstein 2023); **yardline rounding** to integers overstates optimal aggressiveness (Lopez 2020); and WP-based policies **understate uncertainty** (Brill–Yurko–Wyner 2023), so small go-boost edges should not be treated as sharp. Note the conceptual point from Sandholtz et al.: coaches behave as if optimizing *low quantiles* of the outcome distribution (conservative risk preferences), so a WP-maximizing engine will systematically disagree with observed coaching — that gap is the model's edge, not a bug.

### Implementation takeaway for the engine

This section matters less as a bet-prediction input and more as a **coaching-decision adjustment**: in-game and pre-game models should price fourth-down behavior from WP-maximization, not from league-average coach behavior, because the literature shows average coaching leaves ~0.4 wins/year on the table. For the engine: add a "fourth-down aggressiveness" team/coach feature (actual go rate vs WP-optimal go rate), and in live betting use the go/punt/FG WP differentials as situation features. If rebuilding the decision model, replicate nfl4th's architecture (action-specific outcome distributions → expected WP → argmax) and carry its documented limitations.

### Verification status

- VERIFIED (official package site): the three submodels' contents (go = yards-gained distribution + defensive-penalty first downs; punt = blocks/return TDs/fumbled returns; FG = distance + roof type), the recommendation rule (highest expected WP), and the stated limitations.
- VERIFIED (academic, 2024): nfl4th's WP model underlies the decision engine; the literature chain (Romer → Burke → Baldwin → Yam & Lopez → Daly-Grafstein → Lopez → Brill/Yurko/Wyner → Roach & Owens) with the specific corrections each adds.
- PARTIAL: CRAN dependencies include XGBoost and GAM tooling, but I could not confirm from readable sources which submodel uses which model class — do not assert it. Exact current training windows/calibration procedure are UNVERIFIED.
